title: Stochastic Verification + Safety + Knowledge Stages
description: Wire Phase 4 (stochastic verification) and Phase 5 (safety + knowledge) into the pipeline. Phase 4 runs Monte Carlo simulations to produce confidence intervals on all predictions — force, temperature, surface finish, dimensional accuracy, and process robustness. Phase 5 applies 24 safety rules, 296 playbook rules, 2,800+ tribal knowledge tips, reliability checks, energy optimization, and acoustic analysis. Together these phases ensure the output is not just fast but SAFE and PROVEN.

units.title: Stage 4.1-4.2 — Monte Carlo process simulation + Uncertainty propagation
steps: Wire StochasticCuttingForceEngine: MC simulation of force distribution per block
Input uncertainty sources: material property spread (±5-15%), tool geometry tolerance, machine positioning error, runout TIR
Use MaterialBatchVariabilityEngine: Cholesky-correlated material properties (UTS/hardness/thermal_cond are correlated, not independent)
Wire UncertaintyPropagationPipelineEngine: propagate distributions through Force→Deflection→Dimension→Cpk chain
Output: 95% confidence intervals on all key outputs (force, temperature, deflection, surface finish, dimensional accuracy)
Use LHS (Latin Hypercube Sampling) for efficiency — 500 samples gives good convergence
Store CI bounds in PipelineContext for each block
exit_conditions: Every cutting block has force CI (5th/95th percentile)
CI width increases with uncertainty in input parameters
Correlated inputs produce tighter CIs than independent assumption
500 LHS samples converge within 2% of 10,000-sample reference

units.title: Stage 4.3-4.5 — Dimensional + Surface finish + Environmental verification
steps: Wire StochasticDimensionalEngine: predict dimensional distribution from force/deflection/thermal/machine error sources
Calculate P(dimension within tolerance) for each critical feature
Wire StochasticSurfaceFinishEngine: predict Ra/Rz distribution from fz, corner radius, BUE probability, vibration
Verify Ra target achievable with predicted S/F — if P(Ra > target) > 5%, reduce feed
Wire EnvironmentalVariationEngine: shop temperature (±3°C diurnal) + humidity impact on dimensions
CTE mismatch: workpiece expands differently than machine at non-20°C temperatures
For precision work (Cpk target > 1.67): environmental variation can be the dominant error source
exit_conditions: Dimensional probability calculated for user-specified tolerances
Surface finish target verified against predicted Ra distribution
Environmental variation measurably affects Cpk for tight tolerances
Warning generated when P(out_of_spec) > 5%

units.title: Stage 4.6-4.7 — Material batch variability + Process robustness score
steps: Wire MaterialBatchVariabilityEngine: heat-to-heat property variation for 9+ material families
Bayesian certification: if user has material cert data, use actual values; else use distribution from material grade spec
Wire ProcessRobustnessEngine: Taguchi signal-to-noise ratio for the entire parameter set
Identify most sensitive parameters (Sobol Si from StochasticWrapperEngine)
Report: 'Feed rate is responsible for 45% of dimensional variation — tighten feed control'
Overall robustness score: 0-100 (100 = insensitive to all variation sources)
If robustness < 60, suggest parameter adjustments to improve (reduce speed to more robust zone)
exit_conditions: Material batch variation produces realistic property spreads
Sobol sensitivity indices identify top 3 variation drivers
Robustness score correlates with CI width (wider CIs = lower robustness)
Actionable recommendations generated for low-robustness setups
25+ tests across Phase 4 stages

units.title: Stage 5.1-5.2 — G-code safety analysis + Playbook rules application
steps: Wire GCodeSafetyAnalyzerEngine: 24 safety rules applied to generated G-code
Machine envelope check: verify all moves within machine work volume
Feed/speed limit check: verify S/F within machine and tool maximums
Tool number/offset validation: verify tool numbers exist in machine magazine
Rapid move safety: verify rapids don't intersect stock/fixtures (when geometry available)
Wire MachiningPlaybookEngine: 296 rules across 42 categories
Material-specific rules: e.g., MAT-001 (stainless: avoid dwelling), MAT-002 (titanium: keep chip moving)
Operation-specific rules: e.g., threading rules, deep hole rules, HSM rules
Anti-pattern detection: flood coolant + carbide at low speed (ANTI-004), interrupted cut + CBN, etc.
Apply rule overrides to S/F where rules conflict with physics stage output
exit_conditions: All 24 safety rules evaluated on output G-code
Playbook rules fire for material-specific conditions
Anti-pattern warnings generated with remediation
Safety violations block output with CRITICAL severity

units.title: Stage 5.3-5.6 — Tribal knowledge + Reliability + Energy + Acoustics
steps: Wire tribal knowledge lookup: query 2,800+ tips filtered by CAM system + material + operation
Include CAM-system-specific warnings (e.g., Fusion 360 arc tolerance issues, hyperMILL TCPM settings)
Include controller-specific tips (e.g., Haas G187 mode selection, Fanuc macro variable limits)
Wire MinerCumulativeDamageEngine: check cumulative fatigue on tool across program (Palmgren-Miner)
If cumulative damage > 0.8, recommend tool change or reduced parameters
Wire GCodeEnergyOptimizerEngine: optimize idle time, coolant pump cycling, spindle on/off
Idle spindle detection: if spindle runs during rapid traverse > 3 seconds, suggest M5/M3 bracketing
Wire MachiningAcousticsEngine: predict noise level from cutting parameters
If predicted dB > 85 (OSHA limit), include hearing protection advisory in setup sheet
All knowledge-stage outputs are advisory (warnings), not blocking
exit_conditions: Tribal knowledge tips contextually relevant to the job (not generic)
Tool fatigue damage accumulated across all operations with same tool
Energy optimization reduces estimated power consumption by measurable amount
Noise advisory generated for high-speed/high-engagement operations
20+ tests across Phase 5 stages
